pages.text: Buns steamed in the kitchen pot. Kota stood close and peeked under the lid. Steam rushed out.
"Not yet?" A little later, another peek, another rush of steam. Dad looked puzzled. "Why so slow today?"
A frog child hopped outside the kitchen. "Are the buns ready? I'm hungry!" Kota's tummy rumbled, too. They stood sadly together.
Dad sat them before the pot. "Opening the lid lets steam escape and takes longer. Shall we wait for steam's knock?" Both tilted their heads. "Knock?"
The pot began its bubbling song. Kota kept hands on their knees and waited. The urge to open it tingled—but Kota held still.
Then the lid rattled and lifted. "Hear it? Steam's knocking. It means they're ready." Kota and the frog looked at each other. "Bubble, Bubble, Knock, Knock!"
Dad lifted the lid. Clouds of steam rose. White buns had puffed up round! "Wow!" Kota's tail shot up.
Both blew on their buns and bit. "Buns we waited for taste best!" The frog hopped. Kota's cheeks puffed like buns.
Now Kota counted before the pot, hands on knees. "One, listen! Two, steam knocks! Three, yum!" The lid opened only at steam's knock.
That evening, Dad hugged bun-round Kota. "Waiting makes them warmer." Kota patted their belly. "Tomorrow, Bubble, Bubble, Knock, Knock!"
